    public AirMip.PackedMips Packed => _packed;

    public int3 WindowDimsBricks => _windowDimsBricks;
    public int3 WindowDimsChunks => _windowDimsChunks;
    public int3 WindowOrigin => _windowOrigin;
    /// Window origin expressed in BRICKS -- what the shader's bounds guard needs.
    public int3 WindowOriginBricks => _windowOrigin * EngineConfig.CHUNK_EDGE_BRICKS;

    public struct UploadStats
    {
        public int chunksUploaded;
        public int chunksDeferred;
        public int brickRuns;
        /// Dense body SLOTS uploaded this frame, before run-coalescing.
        /// brickRuns/brickSlots is the fragmentation ratio: 1.0 means every
        /// slot became its own SetData call (the free-list is fully scattered),
        /// near 0 means slots are consecutive and collapse into few runs.
        /// Reported because "brick bodies" is the dominant upload phase and
        /// per-call overhead vs bytes-moved are different problems with
        /// different fixes.
        public int brickSlots;
        public int bytesUploaded;
        public int dirtyRemaining;

        // PER-PHASE TIMING. The previous run reported a single upload_ms of
        // 44.9ms median against a 1.0ms budget and gave no way to attribute it.
        // "Where did the 44ms go" is not answerable by adding more Stopwatches
        // around the same call -- it needs the call broken into its parts.
        public double stagingMs;      // building the 4096-entry chunk staging array
        public double clipmapSetMs;   // ClipmapBuffer writes
        public double mipRebuildMs;   // AirMip.RebuildRegion
        public double packRegionMs;   // AirMip.PackRegion
        public double brickSetMs;     // BrickDataBuffer writes (dense bodies)
        public double packUploadMs;   // AirMipPackedBuffer write
        public int setDataCalls;      // count of GPU write calls issued
    }

    /// Use LockBufferForWrite/UnlockBufferAfterWrite instead of SetData for the
    /// per-chunk partial writes.
    ///
    /// WHY THIS IS A TOGGLE AND NOT JUST A CHANGE: SetData with an offset is a
    /// plausible but UNPROVEN suspect for the ~1,000ms/frame that shows up on
    /// the RENDER thread and not in any main-thread Stopwatch. Unity may service
    /// a partial write to an in-flight buffer by renaming the whole allocation --
    /// which for a 384MB BrickDataBuffer would be catastrophic and would land
    /// exactly where the unexplained time is. LockBufferForWrite is the API
    /// intended for partial updates and should avoid that.
    ///
    /// Leaving it switchable so the acceptance rig can A/B it and MEASURE the
    /// difference rather than shipping a fix on a hypothesis. The same pattern
    /// already exists in this file for air-mips (UseLockBufferForAirMip).
    ///
    /// DEFAULT IS false (SetData) BECAUSE THAT IS THE STANDING §3.7 DECISION.
    /// PHASE_1_COMPLETION.md §4 already ran this exact comparison and selected
    /// SetData -- not on a demonstrated win (the ranges overlapped almost
    /// entirely: SetData 16.2-32.9ms, LockBufferForWrite 5.7-32.9ms) but
    /// because the harness was confounded by concurrent render-encoder work
    /// and the result was inconclusive in both directions. That document is
    /// explicit that re-opening the choice requires a properly isolated
    /// re-test, not a flip on a hunch, and the comment above says as much
    /// itself -- LockBufferForWrite is called "a plausible but UNPROVEN
    /// suspect". Shipping true as the default was exactly the flip §4 warned
    /// against. The toggle stays so the rig can still A/B it; the DEFAULT
    /// tracks the decision on record until a measurement overturns it.
    public static bool UseLockBufferForUploads = false;

    /// Skips all GPU writes while leaving every CPU-side structure updated.
    /// Diagnostic only -- lets the rig measure frame time with uploads removed
    /// and nothing else changed, which is the only clean way to separate upload
    /// cost from raymarch cost when the time is hiding on the render thread.
    public static bool SuppressGpuUploads = false;

    public TerrainClipmap(int3 windowChunks, int brickPoolCapacity)
    {
        _windowDimsChunks = windowChunks;
        _windowDimsBricks = windowChunks * EngineConfig.CHUNK_EDGE_BRICKS;
        _brickMask = _windowDimsBricks - new int3(1, 1, 1);
        _chunkMask = windowChunks - new int3(1, 1, 1);

        int totalBricks = _windowDimsBricks.x * _windowDimsBricks.y * _windowDimsBricks.z;

        // LockBufferForWrite usage must be declared at creation. Requesting it
        // unconditionally costs nothing when unused and avoids a second buffer
        // shape to reason about.
        ClipmapBuffer = new GraphicsBuffer(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured,
            GraphicsBuffer.UsageFlags.LockBufferForWrite, totalBricks, 4);
        BrickDataBuffer = new GraphicsBuffer(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured,
            GraphicsBuffer.UsageFlags.LockBufferForWrite, brickPoolCapacity * 128, 4);
        _clipmapLocal = new uint[totalBricks];

        // ZERO THE GPU CLIPMAP. This line's absence was the "memory corruption".
        //
        // Incremental upload only ever writes chunks that get LOADED, and a
        // fresh GraphicsBuffer contains whatever was in GPU memory. The window
        // is 32x32 chunks while the load radius covers 27x27, so every slot in
        // the surrounding ring held garbage -- some of it decoding as DENSE
        // handles pointing at arbitrary brick bodies. Rendered as thin plates of
        // random material near y=120..127 voxels, which at distance appear as
        // slabs floating above the horizon.
        //
        // Phase 3 never hit this because its UploadDirty did a full
        // SetData(_clipmapLocal) on every flush, which incidentally zeroed
        // everything. Making the upload incremental removed that side effect and
        // nothing replaced it. _clipmapLocal is already all-zero (uniform air),
        // so one upload at construction establishes the invariant that every
        // slot the shader can address holds a value the CPU agrees with.
        ClipmapBuffer.SetData(_clipmapLocal);

        _mips = AirMip.Build(_clipmapLocal, _windowDimsBricks, NUM_AIR_MIP_LEVELS);
        _airMipBuffers = new GraphicsBuffer[_mips.NumLevels];
        for (int k = 0; k < _mips.NumLevels; k++)
        {
            int count = _mips.Levels[k].Length;
            _airMipBuffers[k] = new GraphicsBuffer(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, count, 4);
            UploadAirMipLevel(k);
        }

        RebuildAndUploadPacked();
        Active = this;
    }

    public void SetWindowOrigin(int3 originChunks) => _windowOrigin = originChunks;
    public void MarkDirty(int3 chunkCoord) => _dirtyChunks.Add(chunkCoord);

    // --- Dirty-set introspection. Not decoration: without it a clipmap
    // mismatch is undiagnosable, because "GPU is stale" has two causes that
    // need OPPOSITE fixes:
    //   still dirty  -> upload LAG. The write is queued; the budget or the
    //                   frame ordering delayed it. Benign, or a budget tune.
    //   not dirty    -> LOST UPDATE. Something changed the CPU chunk without
    //                   marking it, or the mark was consumed without the write
    //                   landing. A real bug, and the one that corrupts frames.
    // The first acceptance run reported 15 mismatches and could not tell these
    // apart, which is why it produced no actionable finding.
    public bool IsDirty(int3 chunkCoord) => _dirtyChunks.Contains(chunkCoord);
    public int DirtyCount => _dirtyChunks.Count;

    /// Forces every pending chunk out regardless of the per-frame byte budget.
    /// Test/diagnostic use only -- it deliberately violates §0.2's anti-stutter
    /// cap, which is exactly why it must never be called from a timing path.
    public UploadStats FlushAllDirty(ChunkStore store, BrickDataPool cpuPool)
        => UploadDirty(store, cpuPool, int.MaxValue, int3.zero, int.MaxValue);

    // =========================================================================
    // Indexing
    // =========================================================================

    /// Ring slot for a chunk. Origin-independent for the same reason
    /// ChunkStore.GetFlatIndex is: under a power-of-two mask, subtracting the
    /// origin only rotates the ring. The origin matters for BOUNDS, not index.
    private int ChunkSlot(int3 chunkCoord)
    {
        int3 w = chunkCoord & _chunkMask;
        return w.x + _windowDimsChunks.x * (w.y + _windowDimsChunks.y * w.z);
    }

    /// Brick-linear index into the CPU-side mirror that feeds AirMip. NOT the
    /// GPU layout -- keep the two straight, they are deliberately different.
    private int BrickLinearIndex(int3 worldBrick)
    {
        int3 w = worldBrick & _brickMask;
        return w.x + (w.y * _windowDimsBricks.x) + (w.z * _windowDimsBricks.x * _windowDimsBricks.y);
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // Upload
    // =========================================================================

    /// Phase 2/3 compatibility overload: unbudgeted, uploads everything dirty.
    /// Used by the Phase 2/3 bootstrappers, which populate a static world once
    /// and are not subject to a per-frame budget.
    public void UploadDirty(ChunkStore store, BrickDataPool cpuPool)
        => UploadDirty(store, cpuPool, int.MaxValue, int3.zero, int.MaxValue);

    public UploadStats UploadDirty(ChunkStore store, BrickDataPool cpuPool,
        int byteBudget, int3 cameraChunk, int exemptRadiusChunks)
    {
        var stats = new UploadStats();
        if (_dirtyChunks.Count == 0) return stats;

        var sw = System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.StartNew();
        double phaseStart = 0;

        // Exempt chunks first (§3.7's 8.4 invariant), then the rest nearest-first
        // so the spread admits what the player is closest to seeing.
        _dirtyOrdered.Clear();
        _dirtyOrdered.AddRange(_dirtyChunks);
        _dirtyOrdered.Sort((a, b) => ChebyshevXZ(a, cameraChunk).CompareTo(ChebyshevXZ(b, cameraChunk)));

        _dirtyBrickSlots.Clear();
        int bytes = 0;

        // §0.2's cap has to bound EVERY byte this frame puts on the bus. It did
        // not: only the clipmap-ENTRY term was tested in the loop below, while
        // the two larger payloads -- the dense 512B brick bodies flushed by
        // UploadDirtyBrickBodies, and this packed air-mip SetData -- are added
        // to `bytes` AFTER the loop has already made every admission decision.
        // Both bypassed the budget completely, which is why Gate C measured a
        // ~3.28MB peak against the 3.145MB cap while the entry term alone was
        // bounded to 256KB by MAX_CLIPMAP_CHUNKS_PER_FRAME and could never have
        // breached it on its own. Charged up front so a chunk is admitted only
        // when its FULL cost fits.
        int packedReserve = (_packed != null && !SuppressGpuUploads)
            ? _packed.Words.Length * 4
            : 0;

        // The BYTE cap alone was not a throttle. 3 MB / 16 KB per chunk = 192
        // chunks per frame, and each chunk costs a 4096-iteration staging loop,
        // an AirMip.RebuildRegion, a PackRegion and a SetData -- CPU work that
        // dwarfs the bus traffic the byte cap was written to bound. §0.2's cap
        // protects the bus; this one protects the frame.
        int chunkCap = byteBudget == int.MaxValue
            ? int.MaxValue
            : EngineConfig.MAX_CLIPMAP_CHUNKS_PER_FRAME;

        foreach (int3 chunkCoord in _dirtyOrdered)
        {
            Chunk chunk = store.GetChunk(chunkCoord);
            bool exempt = ChebyshevXZ(chunkCoord, cameraChunk) <= exemptRadiusChunks;

            // Deferred chunks stay in _dirtyChunks and upload on a later frame
            // -- that IS §3.7's multi-frame spread, not a dropped write, and the
            // rig's "no LOST UPDATES" check covers the difference.
            //
            // Exempt chunks are still unconditional (§3.7's 8.4 invariant: what
            // the player stands in or just edited uploads THIS frame). They are
            // therefore still able to carry the total past the cap on their own;
            // bounding them would mean breaking that invariant, which is not a
            // trade this fix is allowed to make.
            if (!exempt)
            {
                int committed = bytes
                              + _dirtyBrickSlots.Count * EngineConfig.BRICK_BODY_BYTES
                              + packedReserve;
                int chunkCost = EngineConfig.CLIPMAP_BYTES_PER_CHUNK
                              + ProjectedBodyBytes(chunk);
                if (committed + chunkCost > byteBudget
                    || stats.chunksUploaded >= chunkCap)
                { stats.chunksDeferred++; continue; }
            }

            phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;
            int3 baseBrickCoord = chunkCoord * EngineConfig.CHUNK_EDGE_BRICKS;

            // A dirty chunk that is NO LONGER RESIDENT has been evicted, and it
            // must be CLEARED, not skipped.
            //
            // This was the terrain-holes bug. Skipping left the GPU holding that
            // chunk's 4096 handles, still pointing at pool slots that
            // ChunkStore.EvictChunk had already returned to the free-list and
            // that a different chunk had since been given. Worse, the air-mip
            // still described the region, so rays either leapt through solid
            // terrain (holes) or hit freed bodies (garbage geometry).
            //
            // It is reachable, not theoretical: the window spans
            // camChunk-16..camChunk+15 while eviction fires beyond radius 15, so
            // evicted slots sit INSIDE the window bounds where the shader's
            // guard lets the read through.
            //
            // Clearing to uniform air is correct rather than merely safe: an
            // unloaded chunk reads as air on the CPU too (see ChunkStore's
            // GetVoxel note), so the two mirrors agree.
            bool evicted = chunk == null;

            for (int z = 0; z < 16; z++)
            for (int y = 0; y < 16; y++)
            for (int x = 0; x < 16; x++)
            {
                int3 localBrick = new int3(x, y, z);
                int local = CoordMath.LocalBrickIndex(localBrick);

                uint handle;
                if (evicted) handle = 0u;                        // uniform air
                else if (chunk.isUniform) handle = chunk.uniformMaterial;
                else handle = chunk.bricks[local].data;

                _chunkStaging[local] = handle;
                _clipmapLocal[BrickLinearIndex(baseBrickCoord + localBrick)] = handle;

                if ((handle & 0x80000000u) != 0)
                    _dirtyBrickSlots.Add((int)(handle & 0x3FFFFFFFu));
            }

            stats.stagingMs += sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
            phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;

            // ONE contiguous write per chunk -- the whole point of chunk-major.
            WriteClipmapChunk(ChunkSlot(chunkCoord) * EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK, ref stats);

            stats.clipmapSetMs += sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
            phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;

            int3 regionMax = baseBrickCoord + new int3(15, 15, 15);
            AirMip.RebuildRegion(_clipmapLocal, _mips, baseBrickCoord, regionMax);

            stats.mipRebuildMs += sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
            phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;
            // Keep the packed mirror in lockstep with the pyramid, incrementally.
            // Was a full AirMip.Pack() once per frame: ~2.4M cells rescanned and
            // a fresh ~300 KB array allocated, every frame that uploaded
            // anything. See AirMip.PackRegion.cs.
            AirMip.PackRegion(_packed, _mips, baseBrickCoord, regionMax);

            stats.packRegionMs += sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
            phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;

            _dirtyChunks.Remove(chunkCoord);
            stats.chunksUploaded++;
            bytes += EngineConfig.CLIPMAP_BYTES_PER_CHUNK;
        }

        phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;
        bytes += UploadDirtyBrickBodies(cpuPool, ref stats);
        stats.brickSetMs = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
        phaseStart = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds;

        if (stats.chunksUploaded > 0)
        {
            if (UseLegacyAirMipUpload)
                for (int k = 0; k < _mips.NumLevels; k++) UploadAirMipLevel(k);

            // Upload only. The words were already updated in place by
            // PackRegion above; the whole packed pyramid is ~300 KB at the
            // Phase 4 mirror size, so one SetData is cheaper than tracking which
            // word ranges are dirty.
            if (_packed != null && !SuppressGpuUploads)
            {
                AirMipPackedBuffer.SetData(_packed.Words);
                stats.setDataCalls++;
                bytes += _packed.Words.Length * 4;
            }
        }

        stats.packUploadMs = sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - phaseStart;
        stats.bytesUploaded = bytes;
        stats.dirtyRemaining = _dirtyChunks.Count;
        return stats;
    }

    private void WriteClipmapChunk(int dstElement, ref UploadStats stats)
    {
        if (SuppressGpuUploads) return;
        stats.setDataCalls++;

        if (UseLockBufferForUploads)
        {
            var na = ClipmapBuffer.LockBufferForWrite<uint>(dstElement, EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK);
            na.CopyFrom(_chunkStaging);
            ClipmapBuffer.UnlockBufferAfterWrite<uint>(EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK);
        }
        else
        {
            ClipmapBuffer.SetData(_chunkStaging, 0, dstElement, EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK);
        }
    }

    private void WriteBrickRun(NativeArray<uint> src, int firstUint, int countUints, ref UploadStats stats)
    {
        if (SuppressGpuUploads) return;
        stats.setDataCalls++;

        if (UseLockBufferForUploads)
        {
            var na = BrickDataBuffer.LockBufferForWrite<uint>(firstUint, countUints);
            NativeArray<uint>.Copy(src, firstUint, na, 0, countUints);
            BrickDataBuffer.UnlockBufferAfterWrite<uint>(countUints);
        }
        else
        {
            BrickDataBuffer.SetData(src, firstUint, firstUint, countUints);
        }
    }

    /// Uploads only the dense bodies the dirty chunks reference. Sorts the
    /// slot indices and coalesces consecutive ones into single ranges: a
    /// freshly generated chunk allocates its slots consecutively (BrickDataPool
    /// hands out a descending free-stack, so sequential Allocs are sequential
    /// indices), which collapses hundreds of slots into a few runs.
    /// Bytes of dense brick BODY that uploading this chunk would add, counted
    /// read-only so a deferred chunk mutates nothing. An evicted chunk uploads
    /// as uniform air and a uniform chunk owns no bodies, so both cost zero and
    /// skip the scan entirely. The count is an upper bound on what
    /// UploadDirtyBrickBodies will actually write (its run-coalescing collapses
    /// duplicates), which is the conservative direction for a cap.
    private static int ProjectedBodyBytes(Chunk chunk)
    {
        if (chunk == null || chunk.isUniform) return 0;

        int dense = 0;
        BrickHandle[] bricks = chunk.bricks;
        for (int i = 0; i < EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK; i++)
            if ((bricks[i].data & 0x80000000u) != 0) dense++;

        return dense * EngineConfig.BRICK_BODY_BYTES;
    }

    private int UploadDirtyBrickBodies(BrickDataPool cpuPool, ref UploadStats stats)
    {
        if (_dirtyBrickSlots.Count == 0) return 0;

        _dirtyBrickSlots.Sort();
        stats.brickSlots = _dirtyBrickSlots.Count;

        // Reinterpret the byte pool as uints so source and destination strides
        // agree with the buffer's 4-byte element size. 512 bytes = 128 uints.
        NativeArray<uint> asUints = cpuPool.RawData.Reinterpret<uint>(sizeof(byte));

        int bytes = 0;
        int i = 0;
        while (i < _dirtyBrickSlots.Count)
        {
            int runStart = _dirtyBrickSlots[i];
            int runEnd = runStart;
            i++;
            while (i < _dirtyBrickSlots.Count &&
                   (_dirtyBrickSlots[i] == runEnd || _dirtyBrickSlots[i] == runEnd + 1))
            {
                runEnd = _dirtyBrickSlots[i];
                i++;
            }

            int firstUint = runStart * 128;
            int countUints = (runEnd - runStart + 1) * 128;
            WriteBrickRun(asUints, firstUint, countUints, ref stats);

            stats.brickRuns++;
            bytes += countUints * 4;
        }

        _dirtyBrickSlots.Clear();
        return bytes;
    }

    private static int ChebyshevXZ(int3 a, int3 b)
        => math.max(math.abs(a.x - b.x), math.abs(a.z - b.z));

    /// Full rebuild + upload. Construction only -- the per-frame path uses
    /// AirMip.PackRegion instead.
    private void RebuildAndUploadPacked()
    {
        _packed = AirMip.Pack(_mips);

        if (AirMipPackedBuffer == null || AirMipPackedBuffer.count != _packed.Words.Length)
        {
            AirMipPackedBuffer?.Release();
            AirMipPackedBuffer = new GraphicsBuffer(GraphicsBuffer.Target.Structured, _packed.Words.Length, 4);
        }
        AirMipPackedBuffer.SetData(_packed.Words);
    }

    private void UploadAirMipLevel(int k)
    {
        uint[] level = _mips.Levels[k];
        if (UseLockBufferForAirMip)
        {
            var native = _airMipBuffers[k].LockBufferForWrite<uint>(0, level.Length);
            native.CopyFrom(level);
            _airMipBuffers[k].UnlockBufferAfterWrite<uint>(level.Length);
        }
        else
        {
            _airMipBuffers[k].SetData(level);
        }
    }

    /// Exposed for ClipmapValidator, which must reproduce the GPU index exactly
    /// rather than keeping its own copy of the formula -- the failure mode its
    /// own header already records ("each had their own copy of the window size,
    /// and only the first two happened to agree").
    public int GpuIndexOf(int3 chunkCoord, int3 localBrick)
        => ChunkSlot(chunkCoord) * EngineConfig.BRICKS_PER_CHUNK + CoordMath.LocalBrickIndex(localBrick);

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (Active == this) Active = null;
        ClipmapBuffer?.Release();
        BrickDataBuffer?.Release();
        AirMipPackedBuffer?.Release();
        AirMipPackedBuffer = null;
        if (_airMipBuffers != null)
        {
            for (int k = 0; k < _airMipBuffers.Length; k++) _airMipBuffers[k]?.Release();
            _airMipBuffers = null;
        }
    }
}

// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/Raymarch.compute
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/Raymarch.compute
//
// AMENDMENT 8.9 / §6.4 LOD CASCADE ADDITION:
// New buffers/params for cascade tiers 1-2, and a new coarse-tier traversal
// branch, ALL gated behind _UseLODCascade (default 0 from C#). When that flag
// is 0, "tier" is forced to 0 every iteration and the ENTIRE original tier-0
// code path below runs completely unchanged - same buffers, same branches,
// same math, byte-for-byte identical to the pre-LOD file. This is deliberate:
// every number in Amendment 8.9 was measured against the old code path, and
// none of that measurement is invalidated by this file until _UseLODCascade
// is explicitly turned on for a new benchmark run.
//
// Coarse-tier design: the ray's DDA state (voxel, tMax, tDelta, step) stays
// in RAW TIER-0 VOXEL UNITS for the whole ray, always. Tiers 1/2 don't get
// their own coordinate space - they just read coarser clipmap/brick buffers
// and treat one coarse brick's span as (8 << tierShift) raw voxels instead of
// 8. This means LeapSpanReseedClosedForm (unchanged, already CPU-fuzz-proven
// per Amendment 8.9 §6) is reused AS-IS for tier 1/2 empty-brick leaps - no
// new DDA math, just a bigger span passed to proven code.
//
// KNOWN LIMITATION, FIXED THIS PASS (was open, now resolved - see chat): the
// coarse-tier dense-brick path used to step ONE RAW VOXEL at a time even
// though a tier-2 coarse voxel is 4 raw voxels wide, costing up to 4
// iterations per coarse voxel crossed instead of 1. A real benchmark
// (Mode4-DenseSkip, cascade ON vs OFF, same pose) measured this costing
// ~83% - nearly 2x - before the fix, confirming the file's own earlier
// prediction. Fixed by leaping the full raw-voxel span of an air coarse
// voxel via the same already-proven LeapSpanReseedClosedForm the empty-
// brick case already used, just with a one-coarse-voxel-sized span instead
// of a whole-brick-sized one. See the tier>0 dense branch below for the
// exact change. NOT yet re-measured after this fix - that's the next
// verification step, not something to assume from the reasoning alone.
//
// STILL OPEN, NOT ADDRESSED THIS PASS: tiers 1/2 still have no air-mip
// pyramid equivalent - empty coarse BRICKS are still skipped one brick at a
// time (see the empty-brick leap below), with no multi-level hierarchy to
// leap across many bricks at once the way tier 0's pyramid does. If the fix
// above isn't enough on its own to close the gap with cascade-off, this is
// the next thing to build, not a smaller tweak to the fix above.
#pragma kernel CSMain

#include "../Coord/CoordMath.hlsl"
#include "../Memory/StructHeaders.hlsl"

RWTexture2D<float4> ResultTexture;
StructuredBuffer<uint> ClipmapBuffer;
StructuredBuffer<uint> BrickDataBuffer;

// --- LOD CASCADE: tier 1 (0.2m) and tier 2 (0.4m) clipmap + brick data ---
// Bound even when _UseLODCascade==0 (RaymarchFeature falls back to binding
// the tier-0 buffers as harmless dummies in that case, same pattern already
// used for AirMip2-4 when fewer levels are built) so the shader never reads
// an unset buffer.
StructuredBuffer<uint> ClipmapBufferTier1;
StructuredBuffer<uint> BrickDataBufferTier1;
StructuredBuffer<uint> ClipmapBufferTier2;
StructuredBuffer<uint> BrickDataBufferTier2;
uint4 _WindowDimsCoarseBricksTier1; // .xyz = coarse-brick dims, .w unused
uint4 _WindowDimsCoarseBricksTier2;

// .x = tier0 outer bound, .y = tier1 outer bound, .z = tier2 outer bound (the
// true ray-travel cap when cascade is active), .w unused. All in RAW VOXEL
// UNITS (meters * 10), matching currentDist's units. Set from
// LODConfig.TIER_OUTER_RANGE_M by RaymarchFeature - this shader has no
// knowledge of the meter values itself, only the voxel-unit conversion.
float4 _TierOuterRangeVoxels;
int _UseLODCascade;

// --- AIR-MIP: legacy four-buffer form (modes 0-4) ---
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip1;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip2;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip3;
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMip4;
uint4 _AirMipDims0;
uint4 _AirMipDims1;
uint4 _AirMipDims2;
uint4 _AirMipDims3;
uint  _AirMipLevelCount;

// --- AIR-MIP: packed + merged form (optimization pass) ---
// One buffer, all levels, 1 bit per cell. _MipInfo[k-1] = (dimX, dimY, dimZ,
// wordOffset) for level k. Removes the 4-way dynamic branch over four separate
// buffers AND shrinks the pyramid from ~38 MB to ~1.2 MB so it fits in cache.
StructuredBuffer<uint> AirMipPacked;
float4 _MipInfo[4];
int _UsePackedMips;

float4x4 _CameraInverseProjection;
float4x4 _CameraInverseView;
float3 _CameraPos;
uint4 _WindowDimsBricksPacked;

// --- PHASE 4: sliding window ---
// The clipmap is now CHUNK-MAJOR: flat = chunkSlot*4096 + localBrickIndex.
// See TerrainClipmap.cs's header for the derivation (brick-linear made a
// boundary-crossing slab ~16,000 scattered upload ranges; chunk-major makes it
// 64 contiguous ones).
uint4 _WindowDimsChunksPacked;   // .xyz = window size in CHUNKS

// Minimum corner of the resident window, in BRICKS. Was implicitly (0,0,0)
// while the window was static; the Phase 3 XZ bounds guard said so in its own
// PHASE 4 NOTE. Now supplied by RaymarchFeature every frame.
int4 _WindowOriginBricksPacked;

// Highest world voxel Y that generation can produce content for, +1. Replaces
// the hardcoded 128 in the early-exit below.
//
// DELIBERATELY NOT the window's Y extent. The window reaches 256 voxels at
// WINDOW_CHUNKS_Y=2 but nothing generates above 128, and §6.1 showed grazing
// and sky rays are exactly where the iteration budget goes -- terminating them
// at the CONTENT ceiling rather than the WINDOW ceiling halves their travel.
// Folding this into the window bounds test would be a silent perf regression.
int _ContentCeilingVoxelY;

// Cascade tier geometry: .x = coarse bricks per chunk edge, .y = log2 of that,
// .z = coarse-brick entries per chunk. Tier 1 = (8,3,512), tier 2 = (4,2,64).
uint4 _CascadeTierInfo1;
uint4 _CascadeTierInfo2;

RWStructuredBuffer<float> DebugOut;
uint2 _DebugPixel;

// 0=Beauty 1=StepHeat 2=UniformDense 3=Normals 4=NonExitHeat 5=VoxelGrain 6=LODTier
int4 _DebugModePacked;

int _MaxOuterIterations;

// Max ray travel in VOXELS (128 m = 1280 voxels). Lowering this is the LOD0
// radius trim: the 128 m figure was derived for a 1080p pixel-footprint match,
// so at 960x540 the matched distance is roughly half that. NOTE: with LOD1
// unimplemented (Phase 4), trimming this makes distant terrain vanish rather
// than drop to a coarser level - it measures the cost saving honestly but is
// not a shippable configuration on its own.
// (LOD cascade is now implemented behind _UseLODCascade - when that's on,
// RaymarchFeature overrides the effective max distance to
// _TierOuterRangeVoxels.z instead of using this constant. This field/comment
// is otherwise unchanged so the pre-cascade A/B measurements stay meaningful.)
float _MaxRayDistance;

int _TraversalMode;

// NEW: developer material color palette + per-voxel grain toggle for the
// default Beauty output (DebugMode 0 only - diagnostic views are untouched).
// Defaults ON. Set to 0 to reproduce the original flat-gray Beauty shading
// exactly, byte-for-byte, for any comparison against pre-existing screenshots.
int _UseDevColors;

#define MAX_CHAIN_LEAPS 7

float4 StepHeatColor(int steps)
{
    if (steps <= 24)  return float4(0.0, 0.1, 0.6, 1.0);
    if (steps <= 48)  return float4(0.0, 0.6, 0.2, 1.0);
    if (steps <  96)  return float4(0.8, 0.6, 0.0, 1.0);
    return float4(0.9, 0.05, 0.05, 1.0);
}

float VoxelHash(int3 v)
{
    uint3 uv = (uint3)(v + int3(1 << 20, 1 << 20, 1 << 20));
    uint h = uv.x * 73856093u ^ uv.y * 19349663u ^ uv.z * 83492791u;
    h ^= h >> 13; h *= 1274126177u; h ^= h >> 16;
    return (float)(h & 0xFFFFFFu) / (float)0xFFFFFF;
}

// NEW: developer material palette. 8 hand-picked, well-separated colors,
// cycled by material id (mat-1, since 0 is always air/no-hit and never
// reaches this function). Explicitly a DEBUG palette, not final art -
// picked for maximum distinguishability at low resolution, not for how the
// game should actually look. Swap freely once real material art exists;
// nothing else in the traversal depends on these specific values.
float3 DevMaterialColor(uint mat)
{
    static const float3 kDevPalette[8] = {
        float3(0.85, 0.35, 0.25), // 0: terracotta
        float3(0.35, 0.65, 0.85), // 1: sky blue
        float3(0.45, 0.75, 0.35), // 2: green
        float3(0.85, 0.65, 0.25), // 3: amber
        float3(0.65, 0.35, 0.75), // 4: purple
        float3(0.30, 0.80, 0.75), // 5: teal
        float3(0.80, 0.45, 0.65), // 6: pink
        float3(0.55, 0.55, 0.30), // 7: olive
    };
    uint idx = (mat - 1u) % 8u; // mat is always >=1 here (0/air never hits)
    return kDevPalette[idx];
}

// CHUNK-MAJOR (Phase 4). Ring-masking the CHUNK coord rather than the brick
// coord is what makes a chunk's 4096 entries contiguous. Masking stays
// origin-independent: under a power-of-two mask, subtracting the origin only
// rotates the ring, so the origin is needed for the BOUNDS TEST (in CSMain,
// once per iteration) and not here.
uint ReadClipmap(int3 brickCoord, uint3 windowDimsBricks)
{
    int3 chunkCoord   = brickCoord >> 4;
    int3 wrappedChunk = chunkCoord & (int3)(_WindowDimsChunksPacked.xyz - 1);
    int  chunkSlot    = wrappedChunk.x
                      + (wrappedChunk.y * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x)
                      + (wrappedChunk.z * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.y);

    int3 localBrick = brickCoord & 15;
    int  local      = LocalBrickIndex(localBrick);   // C.1, CoordMath.hlsl

    return ClipmapBuffer[(chunkSlot * 4096) + local];
}

// Generalized clipmap read for cascade tiers 1/2. tierCoarseBrickCoord is in
// THAT TIER's own coarse-brick coordinate space (i.e. already divided down
// to "brick index," not raw voxels) - same convention ReadClipmap uses for
// tier 0. Branches on tier to pick the buffer/dims; tier is derived from
// currentDist so it's coherent across most of a thread group's rays (same
// coherent-branch argument already used for the dense/uniform branch above).
// CHUNK-MAJOR, matching CascadeTierPool. A chunk contributes
// entriesPerChunk contiguous coarse-brick entries (512 at tier 1, 64 at
// tier 2), indexed chunkSlot*entriesPerChunk + local, local x-fastest.
uint ReadClipmapTier(int tier, int3 tierCoarseBrickCoord)
{
    uint4 info = (tier == 1) ? _CascadeTierInfo1 : _CascadeTierInfo2;
    int edge           = (int)info.x;   // coarse bricks per chunk edge
    int edgeShift      = (int)info.y;   // log2(edge)
    int entriesPerChunk= (int)info.z;

    int3 chunkCoord   = tierCoarseBrickCoord >> edgeShift;
    int3 wrappedChunk = chunkCoord & (int3)(_WindowDimsChunksPacked.xyz - 1);
    int  chunkSlot    = wrappedChunk.x
                      + (wrappedChunk.y * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x)
                      + (wrappedChunk.z * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.x * (int)_WindowDimsChunksPacked.y);

    int3 localCoarse = tierCoarseBrickCoord & (edge - 1);
    int  local       = localCoarse.x + edge * (localCoarse.y + edge * localCoarse.z);

    int flatIndex = (chunkSlot * entriesPerChunk) + local;
    return (tier == 1) ? ClipmapBufferTier1[flatIndex] : ClipmapBufferTier2[flatIndex];
}

uint ReadBrickDataTier(int tier, uint poolIdx, uint wordIdx)
{
    if (tier == 1) return BrickDataBufferTier1[(poolIdx * 128) + wordIdx];
    return BrickDataBufferTier2[(poolIdx * 128) + wordIdx];
}

// Tier shift: log2(downsample factor). Tier 1 -> factor 2 -> shift 1.
// Tier 2 -> factor 4 -> shift 2. Matches LODConfig.DownsampleFactor exactly;
// if LODConfig's tier voxel sizes ever change, this must change with it -
// there is deliberately no runtime derivation here (would cost a log2 per
// iteration for a value that's only ever 1 or 2), so this is the one place
// a LODConfig edit requires a matching shader edit.
int TierShift(int tier)
{
    return (tier == 1) ? 1 : 2;
}

int AirMipFlatIndex(int3 cell, uint3 dims)
{
    int3 wrapped = cell & (int3)(dims - 1);
    return wrapped.x
         + wrapped.y * (int)dims.x
         + wrapped.z * (int)dims.x * (int)dims.y;
}

uint ReadAirMipLegacy(int level, int3 cell)
{
    if (level == 1) return AirMip1[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims0.xyz)];
    if (level == 2) return AirMip2[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims1.xyz)];
    if (level == 3) return AirMip3[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims2.xyz)];
    return AirMip4[AirMipFlatIndex(cell, _AirMipDims3.xyz)];
}

// Packed + merged read. One indexed load from one buffer plus a shift/mask -
// no branch over which buffer to hit, and the whole pyramid is small enough
// to stay resident in cache.
uint ReadAirMipPacked(int level, int3 cell)
{
    float4 info = _MipInfo[level - 1];
    uint3 dims = uint3((uint)info.x, (uint)info.y, (uint)info.z);
    int3 wrapped = cell & (int3)(dims - 1);
    int flat = wrapped.x
             + wrapped.y * (int)dims.x
             + wrapped.z * (int)dims.x * (int)dims.y;
    uint wordIdx = (uint)info.w + ((uint)flat >> 5);
    return (AirMipPacked[wordIdx] >> ((uint)flat & 31u)) & 1u;
}

// Dispatches on a UNIFORM, so the branch is scalar and coherent across every
// thread in the dispatch - cheap on Apple GPUs. Note this means the A/B very
// slightly understates the packed path's true benefit, since a dedicated
// packed-only kernel would not carry the dead legacy code at all.
uint ReadAirMip(int level, int3 cell)
{
    if (_UsePackedMips != 0) return ReadAirMipPacked(level, cell);
    return ReadAirMipLegacy(level, cell);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//  mode 0 leap (unchanged)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
void LeapSpan(inout int3 voxel, inout float3 tMax, inout float currentDist,
              float3 tDelta, int3 step, int3 spanMin, int spanVoxels, inout int3 normal,
              inout int exitIters, inout int nonExitIters)
{
    int3 exitCount = int3(
        step.x > 0 ? (spanMin.x + spanVoxels - voxel.x) : (voxel.x - (spanMin.x - 1)),
        step.y > 0 ? (spanMin.y + spanVoxels - voxel.y) : (voxel.y - (spanMin.y - 1)),
        step.z > 0 ? (spanMin.z + spanVoxels - voxel.z) : (voxel.z - (spanMin.z - 1)));

    precise float tExitX = tMax.x + (exitCount.x - 1) * tDelta.x;
    precise float tExitY = tMax.y + (exitCount.y - 1) * tDelta.y;
    precise float tExitZ = tMax.z + (exitCount.z - 1) * tDelta.z;

    int axis;
    if (tExitX <= tExitY) axis = (tExitX <= tExitZ) ? 0 : 2;
    else                  axis = (tExitY <= tExitZ) ? 1 : 2;

    float tHit = (axis == 0) ? tExitX : ((axis == 1) ? tExitY : tExitZ);

    const float eps = 1e-4;

    int guardX = min(exitCount.x, spanVoxels + 1);
    int guardY = min(exitCount.y, spanVoxels + 1);
    int guardZ = min(exitCount.z, spanVoxels + 1);

    if (axis == 0) { for (int kx = 0; kx < exitCount.x; kx++) { voxel.x += step.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; exitIters++; } }
    if (axis == 1) { for (int ky = 0; ky < exitCount.y; ky++) { voxel.y += step.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; exitIters++; } }
    if (axis == 2) { for (int kz = 0; kz < exitCount.z; kz++) { voxel.z += step.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; exitIters++; } }

    if (axis != 0) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.x <= tHit + eps && g < guardX) { voxel.x += step.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; g++; nonExitIters++; } }
    if (axis != 1) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.y <= tHit + eps && g < guardY) { voxel.y += step.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; g++; nonExitIters++; } }
    if (axis != 2) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.z <= tHit + eps && g < guardZ) { voxel.z += step.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; g++; nonExitIters++; } }

    currentDist = tHit;
    normal = (axis == 0) ? int3(-step.x, 0, 0)
           : ((axis == 1) ? int3(0, -step.y, 0)
                          : int3(0, 0, -step.z));
}

float ReseedTMaxAxis(int voxelAxis, float rayStartAxis, float tDeltaAxis, int stepAxis)
{
    return (stepAxis > 0 ? (voxelAxis + 1.0 - rayStartAxis) : (rayStartAxis - voxelAxis)) * tDeltaAxis;
}

void LeapSpanReseed(inout int3 voxel, inout float3 tMax, inout float currentDist,
                     float3 tDelta, int3 step, float3 rayStart, int3 spanMin, int spanVoxels,
                     inout int3 normal, inout int exitLeaps, inout int nonExitIters)
{
    int3 exitCount = int3(
        step.x > 0 ? (spanMin.x + spanVoxels - voxel.x) : (voxel.x - (spanMin.x - 1)),
        step.y > 0 ? (spanMin.y + spanVoxels - voxel.y) : (voxel.y - (spanMin.y - 1)),
        step.z > 0 ? (spanMin.z + spanVoxels - voxel.z) : (voxel.z - (spanMin.z - 1)));

    precise float tExitX = tMax.x + (exitCount.x - 1) * tDelta.x;
    precise float tExitY = tMax.y + (exitCount.y - 1) * tDelta.y;
    precise float tExitZ = tMax.z + (exitCount.z - 1) * tDelta.z;

    int axis;
    if (tExitX <= tExitY) axis = (tExitX <= tExitZ) ? 0 : 2;
    else                  axis = (tExitY <= tExitZ) ? 1 : 2;

    float tHit = (axis == 0) ? tExitX : ((axis == 1) ? tExitY : tExitZ);

    const float eps = 1e-4;
    int nonExitGuard = spanVoxels + 1;
    int guardX = min(exitCount.x, nonExitGuard);
    int guardY = min(exitCount.y, nonExitGuard);
    int guardZ = min(exitCount.z, nonExitGuard);

    if (axis == 0)
    {
        voxel.x += step.x * exitCount.x;
        tMax.x = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.x, rayStart.x, tDelta.x, step.x);
    }
    if (axis == 1)
    {
        voxel.y += step.y * exitCount.y;
        tMax.y = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.y, rayStart.y, tDelta.y, step.y);
    }
    if (axis == 2)
    {
        voxel.z += step.z * exitCount.z;
        tMax.z = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.z, rayStart.z, tDelta.z, step.z);
    }
    exitLeaps++;

    if (axis != 0) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.x <= tHit + eps && g < guardX) { voxel.x += step.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; g++; nonExitIters++; } }
    if (axis != 1) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.y <= tHit + eps && g < guardY) { voxel.y += step.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; g++; nonExitIters++; } }
    if (axis != 2) { int g = 0; [loop] while (tMax.z <= tHit + eps && g < guardZ) { voxel.z += step.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; g++; nonExitIters++; } }

    currentDist = tHit;
    normal = (axis == 0) ? int3(-step.x, 0, 0)
           : ((axis == 1) ? int3(0, -step.y, 0)
                          : int3(0, 0, -step.z));
}

void LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(inout int3 voxel, inout float3 tMax, inout float currentDist,
                     float3 tDelta, int3 step, float3 rayStart, int3 spanMin, int spanVoxels,
                     inout int3 normal, inout int exitLeaps, inout int nonExitIters)
{
    int3 exitCount = int3(
        step.x > 0 ? (spanMin.x + spanVoxels - voxel.x) : (voxel.x - (spanMin.x - 1)),
        step.y > 0 ? (spanMin.y + spanVoxels - voxel.y) : (voxel.y - (spanMin.y - 1)),
        step.z > 0 ? (spanMin.z + spanVoxels - voxel.z) : (voxel.z - (spanMin.z - 1)));

    precise float tExitX = tMax.x + (exitCount.x - 1) * tDelta.x;
    precise float tExitY = tMax.y + (exitCount.y - 1) * tDelta.y;
    precise float tExitZ = tMax.z + (exitCount.z - 1) * tDelta.z;

    int axis;
    if (tExitX <= tExitY) axis = (tExitX <= tExitZ) ? 0 : 2;
    else                  axis = (tExitY <= tExitZ) ? 1 : 2;

    float tHit = (axis == 0) ? tExitX : ((axis == 1) ? tExitY : tExitZ);

    const float eps = 1e-4;
    int nonExitGuard = spanVoxels + 1;
    int guardX = min(exitCount.x, nonExitGuard);
    int guardY = min(exitCount.y, nonExitGuard);
    int guardZ = min(exitCount.z, nonExitGuard);

    if (axis == 0) voxel.x += step.x * exitCount.x;
    if (axis == 1) voxel.y += step.y * exitCount.y;
    if (axis == 2) voxel.z += step.z * exitCount.z;
    exitLeaps++;

    if (axis != 0)
    {
        float absDirX = 1.0 / tDelta.x;
        int nx = (int)floor((tHit + eps - tMax.x) * absDirX) + 1;
        nx = clamp(nx, 0, guardX);
        voxel.x += step.x * nx;
        nonExitIters += nx;
    }
    if (axis != 1)
    {
        float absDirY = 1.0 / tDelta.y;
        int ny = (int)floor((tHit + eps - tMax.y) * absDirY) + 1;
        ny = clamp(ny, 0, guardY);
        voxel.y += step.y * ny;
        nonExitIters += ny;
    }
    if (axis != 2)
    {
        float absDirZ = 1.0 / tDelta.z;
        int nz = (int)floor((tHit + eps - tMax.z) * absDirZ) + 1;
        nz = clamp(nz, 0, guardZ);
        voxel.z += step.z * nz;
        nonExitIters += nz;
    }

    tMax.x = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.x, rayStart.x, tDelta.x, step.x);
    tMax.y = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.y, rayStart.y, tDelta.y, step.y);
    tMax.z = ReseedTMaxAxis(voxel.z, rayStart.z, tDelta.z, step.z);

    currentDist = tHit;
    normal = (axis == 0) ? int3(-step.x, 0, 0)
           : ((axis == 1) ? int3(0, -step.y, 0)
                          : int3(0, 0, -step.z));
}

[numthreads(8, 8, 1)]
void CSMain(uint3 id : SV_DispatchThreadID)
{
    uint3 _WindowDimsBricks = _WindowDimsBricksPacked.xyz;
    int _DebugMode = _DebugModePacked.x;

    uint width, height;
    ResultTexture.GetDimensions(width, height);
    if (id.x >= width || id.y >= height) return;

    bool isDebugPixel = (id.x == _DebugPixel.x && id.y == _DebugPixel.y);

    float2 uv = float2((id.x + 0.5) / width, (id.y + 0.5) / height) * 2.0 - 1.0;
    float4 target = mul(_CameraInverseProjection, float4(uv.x, uv.y, 1, 1));
    float3 rayDir = mul(_CameraInverseView, float4(normalize(target.xyz / target.w), 0)).xyz;

    rayDir.x = abs(rayDir.x) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.x >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.x;
    rayDir.y = abs(rayDir.y) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.y >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.y;
    rayDir.z = abs(rayDir.z) < 1e-6 ? (rayDir.z >= 0 ? 1e-6 : -1e-6) : rayDir.z;

    float3 rayStart = _CameraPos * 10.0;

    int3 step = int3(sign(rayDir.x), sign(rayDir.y), sign(rayDir.z));
    float3 tDelta = abs(1.0 / rayDir);

    int3 voxel = WorldToVoxel(_CameraPos);

    float3 tMax = float3(
        step.x > 0 ? (voxel.x + 1.0 - rayStart.x) : (rayStart.x - voxel.x),
        step.y > 0 ? (voxel.y + 1.0 - rayStart.y) : (rayStart.y - voxel.y),
        step.z > 0 ? (voxel.z + 1.0 - rayStart.z) : (rayStart.z - voxel.z)
    ) * tDelta;

    float currentDist = 0;
    int steps = 0;
    bool hit = false;
    uint mat = 0;
    int3 normal = 0;
    bool lastWasDense = false;
    int tierAtHit = 0;

    int exitIters = 0;
    int nonExitIters = 0;
    int chainLeapsTotal = 0;
    int denseMicroSteps = 0;
    int mipProbeCalls = 0;

    if (isDebugPixel)
    {
        DebugOut[0] = rayDir.x; DebugOut[1] = rayDir.y; DebugOut[2] = rayDir.z;
        DebugOut[3] = tDelta.x; DebugOut[4] = tDelta.y; DebugOut[5] = tDelta.z;
    }

    // With cascade OFF (default), _TierOuterRangeVoxels is irrelevant and
    // maxDist behaves exactly as before. With cascade ON, RaymarchFeature
    // sets _MaxRayDistance to _TierOuterRangeVoxels.z itself (the tier-2
    // outer bound), so this line doesn't need its own branch - it already
    // picks up the cascade's true travel limit via the same field.
    float maxDist = (_MaxRayDistance > 0.0) ? _MaxRayDistance : 1280.0;
    int _iterCap = (_MaxOuterIterations > 0) ? _MaxOuterIterations : 400;

    while (currentDist < maxDist && steps < _iterCap)
    {
        // EARLY-EXIT (new, added after real diagnostic data - see chat).
        // Phase2Bootstrapper only EVER generates chunks at cy=0 (world Y in
        // [0, 12.8m) = raw voxel Y in [0, 128)). If the ray is already
        // outside that range and moving FURTHER away (not toward it), every
        // remaining voxel it could ever reach is guaranteed unloaded -
        // ChunkStore.GetVoxel treats a null chunk as air unconditionally.
        // This is not a probabilistic/height-derived bound (which would risk
        // being wrong the way guessed constants have been elsewhere this
        // session) - it's the hard, structural fact of what chunks could
        // possibly exist, so this can never skip a real hit, only a
        // guaranteed miss. StepHeat/LODTierView/UniformDenseView at
        // GroundHorizon showed the cascade's actual dominant added cost is
        // exactly this case: no-hit sky rays now walking to the tier-2 outer
        // bound (290m) instead of the old 128m constant, with nothing to
        // make that walk cheap. This fixes the ROOT case, tier-independent -
        // it fires before tier selection even runs, so it benefits cascade
        // on AND off alike (proportionally far more when cascade is on,
        // given the much longer old maxDist).
        // ASSUMPTION, FLAGGED: breaks if Phase2Bootstrapper ever generates
        // more than cy=0 - the 128 below would need to become the true
        // loaded ceiling instead of this one hardcoded layer's height.
                // ---- CONTENT-CEILING EARLY EXIT (Phase 3, now config-driven) ----
        // Unchanged in behaviour; the hardcoded 128 is now _ContentCeilingVoxelY,
        // set from (MAX_GENERATED_CHUNK_Y+1)*128. Its own Phase 3 comment
        // flagged the constant as an assumption that breaks the moment anything
        // outside cy=0 generates. It stays SEPARATE from, and tighter than, the
        // window bounds test below -- see _ContentCeilingVoxelY's declaration.
        if ((voxel.y >= _ContentCeilingVoxelY && step.y > 0) || (voxel.y < 0 && step.y < 0))
        {
            hit = false;
            break;
        }

        // ---- RESIDENT WINDOW BOUNDS (Phase 4: origin-relative, 3 axes) ----
        // ReadClipmap/ReadClipmapTier mask toroidally with no bounds check, so
        // anything outside the window aliases silently back inside -- the
        // phantom-terrain bug of PHASE_3_COMPLETION.md §6.2. Leaving the window
        // means "no data", which must TERMINATE the ray, never alias into it.
        //
        // ONE guard covers all three tiers. Tiers 1 and 2 cover the same
        // spatial volume as tier 0, sampled coarser, so a voxel inside the
        // tier-0 window is inside theirs by construction. No per-tier origin
        // uniforms are needed and there is deliberately only one bounds site.
        //
        // Placement matters: this must stay the FIRST thing in the loop body,
        // ahead of every clipmap and air-mip read. The tier-1/2 chain loop
        // further down re-reads ReadClipmapTier up to MAX_CHAIN_LEAPS times
        // without re-testing bounds; that is safe ONLY because every exit from
        // that loop returns here before anything is drawn, and because the loop
        // breaks on both dense and uniform-solid handles without setting `hit`.
        {
            int3 rel = VoxelToBrick(voxel) - _WindowOriginBricksPacked.xyz;
            if (rel.x < 0 || rel.y < 0 || rel.z < 0 ||
                rel.x >= (int)_WindowDimsBricks.x ||
                rel.y >= (int)_WindowDimsBricks.y ||
                rel.z >= (int)_WindowDimsBricks.z)
            {
                hit = false;
                break;
            }
        }

        steps++;
        mipProbeCalls++;

        // Tier selection: 0 unless cascade is on AND currentDist has passed
        // that tier's own outer bound. Forced to 0 whenever _UseLODCascade==0,
        // so every line inside "if (tier == 0)" below is reached exactly as
        // it always was - this is the one and only new branch point tier-0
        // rays pass through, and it's a single cheap comparison.
        int tier = 0;
        if (_UseLODCascade != 0)
        {
            if (currentDist >= _TierOuterRangeVoxels.y) tier = 2;
            else if (currentDist >= _TierOuterRangeVoxels.x) tier = 1;
        }

        if (tier == 0)
        {
            // ===================================================================
            // TIER 0 PATH - UNCHANGED from the pre-cascade file. Nothing in this
            // block was touched; it's reproduced verbatim so tier-0-only rays
            // (or any ray when _UseLODCascade==0) get byte-identical behavior.
            // ===================================================================
            bool leapt = false;
            [loop]
            for (int k = (int)_AirMipLevelCount; k >= 1; k--)
            {
                int shift = 3 + k;
                int3 cell = voxel >> shift;
                if (ReadAirMip(k, cell) == 0u)
                {
                    int spanVoxels = 8 << k;
                    int3 spanMin = cell << shift;

                    if (_TraversalMode == 0)
                        LeapSpan(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, spanMin, spanVoxels, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                    else if (_TraversalMode == 3 || _TraversalMode == 4)
                        LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, spanMin, spanVoxels, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                    else
                        LeapSpanReseed(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, spanMin, spanVoxels, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);

                    if (_TraversalMode == 2)
                    {
                        int chainCount = 0;
                        [loop]
                        while (chainCount < MAX_CHAIN_LEAPS)
                        {
                            int3 newCell = voxel >> shift;
                            if (ReadAirMip(k, newCell) != 0u) break;

                            int3 newSpanMin = newCell << shift;
                            LeapSpanReseed(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, newSpanMin, spanVoxels, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                            chainCount++;
                            chainLeapsTotal++;
                        }
                    }

                    leapt = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (leapt) continue;

            int3 brickCoord = VoxelToBrick(voxel);
            uint handle = ReadClipmap(brickCoord, _WindowDimsBricks);
            bool isDense = (handle & 0x80000000) != 0;

            if (isDense)
            {
                uint poolIdx = handle & 0x3FFFFFFF;

                if (_TraversalMode == 4)
                {
                    [loop]
                    while (currentDist < maxDist && steps < _iterCap)
                    {
                        int3 localVoxel = LocalVoxelIndex3D(voxel);
                        uint vIdx = (uint)LocalVoxelIndex(localVoxel);
                        uint packedData = BrickDataBuffer[(poolIdx * 128) + (vIdx >> 2)];
                        uint pShift = (vIdx & 3) * 8;
                        mat = (packedData >> pShift) & 0xFF;

                        if (mat != 0) { hit = true; lastWasDense = true; break; }

                        denseMicroSteps++;
                        steps++;

                        if (tMax.x < tMax.y)
                        {
                            if (tMax.x < tMax.z) { voxel.x += step.x; currentDist = tMax.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; normal = int3(-step.x, 0, 0); }
                            else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
                        }
                        else
                        {
                            if (tMax.y < tMax.z) { voxel.y += step.y; currentDist = tMax.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; normal = int3(0, -step.y, 0); }
                            else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
                        }

                        if (!all(VoxelToBrick(voxel) == brickCoord)) break;
                    }
                    if (hit) { tierAtHit = 0; break; }
                    continue;
                }

                int3 localVoxel2 = LocalVoxelIndex3D(voxel);
                uint vIdx2 = (uint)LocalVoxelIndex(localVoxel2);
                uint packedData2 = BrickDataBuffer[(poolIdx * 128) + (vIdx2 >> 2)];
                uint shift2 = (vIdx2 & 3) * 8;
                mat = (packedData2 >> shift2) & 0xFF;

                if (mat != 0) { hit = true; lastWasDense = true; tierAtHit = 0; break; }

                denseMicroSteps++;
                if (tMax.x < tMax.y)
                {
                    if (tMax.x < tMax.z) { voxel.x += step.x; currentDist = tMax.x; tMax.x += tDelta.x; normal = int3(-step.x, 0, 0); }
                    else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
                }
                else
                {
                    if (tMax.y < tMax.z) { voxel.y += step.y; currentDist = tMax.y; tMax.y += tDelta.y; normal = int3(0, -step.y, 0); }
                    else                 { voxel.z += step.z; currentDist = tMax.z; tMax.z += tDelta.z; normal = int3(0, 0, -step.z); }
                }
                continue;
            }

            mat = handle & 0xFF;
            if (mat != 0) { hit = true; lastWasDense = false; tierAtHit = 0; break; }

            {
                int3 bMin = brickCoord * 8;
                if (_TraversalMode == 0)
                    LeapSpan(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, bMin, 8, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                else if (_TraversalMode == 3 || _TraversalMode == 4)
                    LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, bMin, 8, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                else
                    LeapSpanReseed(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, bMin, 8, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
            }
        }
        else
        {
            // ===================================================================
            // TIER 1 / TIER 2 PATH - new. Only reached when _UseLODCascade!=0
            // AND currentDist has already passed tier 0's (and possibly tier
            // 1's) outer bound. No air-mip pyramid exists for these tiers yet
            // (deliberate scope cut for this pass - flagged in the file header
            // and in chat) - empty coarse bricks are skipped one brick at a
            // time via LeapSpanReseedClosedForm instead, same as tier 0's own
            // non-air-mip brick-skip fallback below.
            // ===================================================================
            int tierShift = TierShift(tier); // 1 for tier1, 2 for tier2

            int3 tierVoxel = voxel >> tierShift;
            int3 tierBrickCoord = tierVoxel >> 3;

            uint handle = ReadClipmapTier(tier, tierBrickCoord);
            bool isDense = (handle & 0x80000000) != 0;

            if (isDense)
            {
                uint poolIdx = handle & 0x3FFFFFFF;
                int3 localTierVoxel = tierVoxel & 7;
                uint vIdx = (uint)LocalVoxelIndex(localTierVoxel);
                uint packedData = ReadBrickDataTier(tier, poolIdx, vIdx >> 2);
                uint pShift = (vIdx & 3) * 8;
                mat = (packedData >> pShift) & 0xFF;

                if (mat != 0) { hit = true; lastWasDense = true; tierAtHit = tier; break; }

                // FIX (measured, not guessed): this used to single-step one RAW
                // voxel at a time even though a coarse voxel here spans `factor`
                // (1<<tierShift) raw voxels, all sharing this SAME sampled byte -
                // exactly the "up to 4 iterations, not 1" cost the file header
                // already predicted, now confirmed by a real benchmark (cascade
                // ON measured ~83% SLOWER than cascade OFF at the same pose -
                // see chat). Since every raw voxel within this one coarse voxel
                // is provably the same material (that's what "dense body, one
                // byte per coarse voxel" means), an air coarse voxel (mat==0,
                // this branch) can be leapt in full using the SAME proven
                // LeapSpanReseedClosedForm the empty-brick case below already
                // uses - just with a span of ONE coarse voxel (`factor` raw
                // voxels) instead of one whole brick (8 coarse voxels). No new
                // math, same reused primitive, smaller span.
                {
                    int3 coarseVoxelMinRaw = tierVoxel << tierShift;
                    int coarseVoxelSpanRaw = 1 << tierShift; // = factor: 2 (tier1) or 4 (tier2)
                    LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, coarseVoxelMinRaw, coarseVoxelSpanRaw, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                    denseMicroSteps++;
                }
                continue;
            }

            mat = handle & 0xFF;
            if (mat != 0) { hit = true; lastWasDense = false; tierAtHit = tier; break; }

            // Empty coarse brick: leap its full span using the SAME, UNCHANGED
            // LeapSpanReseedClosedForm tier-0 already uses - just with the span
            // converted back to raw voxel units (8 coarse voxels * factor raw
            // voxels each).
            {
                int3 bMinRaw = (tierBrickCoord * 8) << tierShift;
                int spanVoxelsRaw = 8 << tierShift;
                LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, bMinRaw, spanVoxelsRaw, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);

                // FIX (measured, not guessed - see chat): the prior fix to the
                // dense-voxel-stepping cost barely moved the cascade's overall
                // slowdown (+82.7% -> +77.9%), which means it wasn't the
                // dominant cost at this pose. This is: tiers 1/2 still have no
                // air-mip-equivalent pyramid, so a long empty run gets crossed
                // one brick at a time, each requiring the outer loop to fully
                // re-derive `tier` and re-probe from scratch. Chains ADDITIONAL
                // same-tier empty-brick leaps within this one outer iteration
                // instead - the exact same pattern tier 0's own _TraversalMode
                // == 2 chaining already uses above (MAX_CHAIN_LEAPS), applied
                // here for the first time. Every chained leap re-reads and
                // re-verifies the next brick's handle before leaping it - this
                // is not assuming consecutive bricks are empty, it's confirming
                // each one exactly as the single-leap path already did, just
                // without returning to the outer while loop between them.
                int tierChainCount = 0;
                [loop]
                while (tierChainCount < MAX_CHAIN_LEAPS)
                {
                    // Stop chaining the moment the ray leaves THIS tier's own
                    // distance range - let the outer loop's tier-selection
                    // logic run fresh rather than reading this tier's buffers
                    // past where they're valid.
                    bool stillInThisTier = (tier == 1)
                        ? (currentDist < _TierOuterRangeVoxels.y)
                        : (currentDist < _TierOuterRangeVoxels.z);
                    if (!stillInThisTier) break;

                    int3 nextTierVoxel = voxel >> tierShift;
                    int3 nextTierBrickCoord = nextTierVoxel >> 3;
                    uint nextHandle = ReadClipmapTier(tier, nextTierBrickCoord);

                    if ((nextHandle & 0x80000000) != 0) break; // dense - let the outer loop handle it
                    if ((nextHandle & 0xFF) != 0) break;        // uniform solid - let the outer loop resolve the hit

                    int3 nextBMinRaw = (nextTierBrickCoord * 8) << tierShift;
                    LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(voxel, tMax, currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, nextBMinRaw, spanVoxelsRaw, normal, exitIters, nonExitIters);
                    tierChainCount++;
                    chainLeapsTotal++;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    if (isDebugPixel)
    {
        DebugOut[7] = (float)steps;
        DebugOut[8] = (float)(exitIters + nonExitIters);
        DebugOut[9] = (float)exitIters;
        DebugOut[10] = (float)nonExitIters;
        DebugOut[11] = (float)_TraversalMode;
        DebugOut[12] = (float)chainLeapsTotal;
        DebugOut[13] = (float)denseMicroSteps;
        DebugOut[14] = (float)mipProbeCalls;
        DebugOut[15] = (float)_UsePackedMips;
        DebugOut[16] = maxDist;
        DebugOut[17] = (float)tierAtHit;
        DebugOut[18] = (float)_UseLODCascade;
        // NEW: currentDist at the point the loop exited (hit or maxDist),
        // in RAW VOXEL units (meters * 10) - same units as maxDist/tier
        // boundaries elsewhere in this file. Added specifically to answer
        // "how far away is the pixel that spiked in the diagnostic scan" -
        // see chat - without it, distance had to be estimated from camera
        // geometry instead of measured directly.
        DebugOut[19] = currentDist;
    }

    if (_DebugMode == 1) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = StepHeatColor(steps); return; }
    if (_DebugMode == 2)
    {
        if (!hit) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 1.0); return; }
        ResultTexture[id.xy] = lastWasDense ? float4(0.9, 0.9, 0.2, 1.0) : float4(0.2, 0.2, 0.3, 1.0);
        return;
    }
    if (_DebugMode == 3)
    {
        if (!hit) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0); return; }
        float3 n = (float3(normal) * 0.5) + 0.5;
        ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(n, 1.0);
        return;
    }
    if (_DebugMode == 4) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = StepHeatColor(nonExitIters >> 3); return; }
    if (_DebugMode == 5)
    {
        if (!hit) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0); return; }
        float ndotlV = max(0.25, dot(float3(normal), normalize(float3(0.5, 1.0, 0.2))));
        float baseV = (mat == 2) ? 0.60 : 0.50;
        float variation = (VoxelHash(voxel) - 0.5) * 0.28;
        float shadeV = saturate(baseV + variation) * ndotlV;
        ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(shadeV, shadeV, shadeV, 1.0);
        return;
    }
    if (_DebugMode == 6)
    {
        // LOD tier visualization: NEW. Not hit -> background. Tier 0 -> blue,
        // tier 1 -> green, tier 2 -> red. Purely diagnostic - lets a human
        // eyeball whether tier boundaries land where expected and whether the
        // 0->1->2 transitions are visually reasonable, BEFORE trusting this
        // path for a benchmark run. This is the capture to send back first.
        if (!hit) { ResultTexture[id.xy] = float4(0.05, 0.05, 0.05, 1.0); return; }
        float4 tierColor = float4(0.1, 0.3, 0.9, 1.0); // tier 0 = blue
        if (tierAtHit == 1) tierColor = float4(0.15, 0.85, 0.2, 1.0); // tier 1 = green
        if (tierAtHit == 2) tierColor = float4(0.9, 0.15, 0.15, 1.0); // tier 2 = red
        ResultTexture[id.xy] = tierColor;
        return;
    }

    float4 color = float4(0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0);
    if (hit)
    {
        float ndotl = max(0.2, dot(float3(normal), normalize(float3(0.5, 1.0, 0.2))));
        if (_UseDevColors != 0)
        {
            // NEW: developer material colors + per-voxel grain. Not final art -
            // a cheap, explicitly-flagged debug palette so individual voxels
            // are distinguishable at 960x540, which flat single-shade gray
            // wasn't. Reuses VoxelHash (already existed, was previously only
            // wired into DebugMode 5/VoxelGrain) as the per-voxel noise source -
            // same idea the person asked for ("take the voxel position, apply
            // noise, shift the color slightly"), just extended from grayscale-
            // only to also picking a base hue per material id.
            float3 baseColor = DevMaterialColor(mat);
            float grain = (VoxelHash(voxel) - 0.5) * 0.35; // +/-17.5% per-voxel brightness jitter
            float3 shaded = saturate(baseColor * (1.0 + grain)) * ndotl;
            color = float4(shaded, 1.0);
        }
        else
        {
            // Original flat shading, preserved byte-for-byte behind the
            // toggle - _UseDevColors defaults ON, but flipping it off
            // reproduces every pre-existing Beauty screenshot exactly, for
            // any future A/B comparison that needs the old look specifically.
            color = float4(0.5 * ndotl, 0.5 * ndotl, 0.5 * ndotl, 1.0);
            if (mat == 2) color = float4(0.6 * ndotl, 0.6 * ndotl, 0.6 * ndotl, 1.0);
        }
    }
    ResultTexture[id.xy] = color;
}


// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/RaymarchDenseSkip.cs
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/RaymarchDenseSkip.cs
//
// Amendment 8.9/8.10 - dense-brick mip-reprobe skip.
//
// THE FINDING THIS FIXES: the mineshaft diagnostic (this session) measured
// 18 of 19 outer steps as dense per-voxel micro-steps, each one re-running
// the FULL top-down 4-level air-mip probe before falling through to the
// dense branch - even though the ray was already confirmed inside a dense
// brick and that probe is guaranteed to fail every time until the ray
// actually leaves the brick. The GenerateChunk.cs per-voxel-height fix
// (this session) made this the DEFAULT case along the entire terrain
// surface, not just inside one hand-dug tunnel - every mixed brick at the
// surface now pays this cost on every voxel step, which is why the
// resolution-ladder numbers went up 4x+ after that fix landed.
//
// THE FIX: once a dense brick is entered, stay in a dedicated inner loop
// that steps voxel-by-voxel WITHOUT re-probing the air-mip, until the ray
// actually leaves that brick's bounds. Only then does control return to the
// outer loop, where the mip probe runs again - now against a position where
// the answer can genuinely be different.
//
// WHY THIS IS SAFE - a redundant-check elimination, not a new algorithm:
// while voxel stays inside the SAME dense brick, the air-mip probe's answer
// cannot change. A cell containing a dense (mixed-material) brick is, by
// AirMip's own construction (ReduceFromL0/ReduceFromChild - a cell is air
// iff EVERY covered child is air), not air at ANY level while any part of
// that brick is occupied by this dense handle. So every mip-probe call the
// original code made while stuck inside a known dense brick was doing real
// work to produce an answer that could never change. Skipping those reads
// changes nothing about which voxels get visited, which one produces the
// hit, or what normal/material comes back - it only removes reads that were
// always going to say "not air" anyway.
//
// Same correctness bar as every other tracer in this file: full
// differential fuzz against TracerRaycast (the oracle), final hit/voxel/
// material/normal agreement only - see RaymarchDenseSkipTests.cs.

using Unity.Mathematics;
using VoxelEngine.Memory;

public static partial class RaymarchReference
{
    public static RayHit TracerRaycastMipReseedClosedFormDenseSkip(float3 origin, float3 dir, ChunkStore store,
        AirMipData mips, float maxDist = 128f)
    {
        var (hit, _, _) = TracerRaycastMipReseedClosedFormDenseSkipWithCounts(origin, dir, store, mips, maxDist);
        return hit;
    }

    // Counted variant - exposes how many times the top-down mip probe
    // actually ran (mipProbeCalls) versus how many voxel steps were taken
    // inside the dense-skip inner loop without one (denseSkipSteps). This is
    // the direct proof the optimization fires: on a dense-heavy ray,
    // denseSkipSteps should be large and mipProbeCalls should be small,
    // where the un-optimized ClosedForm tracer would have run the full
    // probe once per voxel step instead.
    public static (RayHit hit, int mipProbeCalls, int denseSkipSteps) TracerRaycastMipReseedClosedFormDenseSkipWithCounts(
        float3 origin, float3 dir, ChunkStore store, AirMipData mips, float maxDist = 128f)
    {
        RayHit result = new RayHit { hit = false, steps = 0 };
        float3 rayStart = origin * 10f;
        float3 rayDir = math.normalize(dir);
        int3 step = (int3)math.sign(rayDir);
        float3 tDelta = math.abs(1f / rayDir);
        int3 voxel = CoordMath.WorldToVoxel(origin);
        float3 tMax = new float3(
            step.x > 0 ? (voxel.x + 1f - rayStart.x) : (rayStart.x - voxel.x),
            step.y > 0 ? (voxel.y + 1f - rayStart.y) : (rayStart.y - voxel.y),
            step.z > 0 ? (voxel.z + 1f - rayStart.z) : (rayStart.z - voxel.z)
        ) * tDelta;
        float currentDist = 0f;
        float maxVoxelDist = maxDist * 10f;
        int3 lastNormal = int3.zero;
        int mipProbeCalls = 0;
        int denseSkipSteps = 0;

        while (currentDist < maxVoxelDist && result.steps < 1000)
        {
            result.steps++;

            byte mat = store.GetVoxel(voxel);
            if (mat != 0)
            {
                result.hit = true;
                result.voxelCoord = voxel;
                result.material = mat;
                result.normal = lastNormal;
                return (result, mipProbeCalls, denseSkipSteps);
            }

            mipProbeCalls++;
            bool leapt = false;
            for (int k = mips.NumLevels; k >= 1; k--)
            {
                int shift = 3 + k;
                int3 cell = voxel >> shift;
                int3 dims = mips.DimsOfLevel(k);
                if (mips.Levels[k - 1][AirMip.FlatIndex(cell, dims)] == 0u)
                {
                    int spanVoxels = 8 << k;
                    int3 spanMin = cell << shift;
                    LeapSpanReseedClosedForm(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step,
                             rayStart, spanMin, spanVoxels, ref lastNormal);
                    leapt = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (leapt) continue;

            int3 brickCoord = CoordMath.VoxelToBrick(voxel);
            if (BrickIsUniformAir(store, brickCoord))
            {
                LeapBrickO1ReseedClosedForm(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step, rayStart, brickCoord, ref lastNormal);
                continue;
            }

            // --- DENSE SKIP: not uniform air, and the check above already
            // found this exact position is air, so this is a genuinely
            // mixed/dense brick. Step voxel by voxel WITHOUT re-probing the
            // air-mip, until the ray actually leaves this brick's bounds. ---
            while (currentDist < maxVoxelDist && result.steps < 1000)
            {
                StepDda(ref voxel, ref tMax, ref currentDist, tDelta, step, ref lastNormal);
                result.steps++;
                denseSkipSteps++;

                byte innerMat = store.GetVoxel(voxel);
                if (innerMat != 0)
                {
                    result.hit = true;
                    result.voxelCoord = voxel;
                    result.material = innerMat;
                    result.normal = lastNormal;
                    return (result, mipProbeCalls, denseSkipSteps);
                }

                if (!CoordMath.VoxelToBrick(voxel).Equals(brickCoord)) break; // left this brick
            }
        }

        return (result, mipProbeCalls, denseSkipSteps);
    }
}

// ==========================================
// FILE: Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/RaymarchFeature.cs
// ==========================================
// ==========================================
// Assets/CoreEngine/Rendering/RaymarchFeature.cs
//
// PHASE 4 REVISION. Additive only -- no traversal behaviour changes. New
// bindings for the sliding window and the chunk-major clipmap layout:
//   _WindowDimsChunksPacked   window size in chunks (chunk-major indexing)
//   _WindowOriginBricksPacked window minimum corner in bricks (bounds guard)
//   _ContentCeilingVoxelY     replaces the hardcoded 128 early-exit
//   _CascadeTierInfo1/2       coarse-brick geometry per cascade tier
// See PATCH_phase4_shaders.md for the matching shader edits.
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.Rendering;
using UnityEngine.Rendering.Universal;
using UnityEngine.Rendering.RenderGraphModule;
using VoxelEngine.Mirror;

public class RaymarchFeature : ScriptableRendererFeature
{
    public enum DebugMode
    {
        Beauty = 0,
        StepHeat = 1,
        UniformDense = 2,
        Normals = 3,
        NonExitHeat = 4,
        VoxelGrain = 5,
        LODTier = 6,
    }

    public enum GateResMode { UseInspector, Native, Forced960x540, ForcedCustom }
    public static GateResMode GateModeOverride = GateResMode.UseInspector;
    public static Vector2Int CustomGateResolution = new Vector2Int(960, 540);

    [Tooltip("Runtime debug view. Beauty is the shipped output.")]
    public DebugMode debugMode = DebugMode.Beauty;

    [Header("Gate measurement resolution")]
    [SerializeField] private bool _forceGateResolution = true;
    [SerializeField] private int _gateWidth = 960;
    [SerializeField] private int _gateHeight = 540;

    public static bool AirMipEnabled = true;

    // CERTIFIED DEFAULT: mode 4 (DenseSkip). Amendment 8.9 recorded it as the
    // fastest measured mode and the one with a CPU oracle fuzz proof.
    public static int TraversalMode = 4;

    // Phase 3 PATCH_iteration_cap: 400 -> 1024. The .compute clamp that pinned
    // the effective cap at 400 was removed in the same patch.
    public static int MaxOuterIterations = 1024;

    public static bool UseStrippedKernel = false;
    public static bool UseMemoryProbeKernel = false;
    public static int ProbeIterations = 14;

    public static bool UsePackedMips = true;
    public static float MaxRayDistance = 1280f;
    public static bool UseLODCascade = true;
    public static bool UseDevColors = true;

    /// Highest world voxel Y that generation can produce content for, +1.
    /// Set by the bootstrapper from StreamManager.MAX_GENERATED_CHUNK_Y.
    /// Kept tighter than the window's Y extent on purpose -- see the shader.
    public static int ContentCeilingVoxelY = 128;

    public static DebugMode DebugViewOverride = DebugMode.Beauty;
    public static bool UseDebugViewOverride = false;

    public static Vector2Int LastDispatchResolution = new Vector2Int(0, 0);

    public static GraphicsBuffer DebugBuffer { get; private set; }
    public static Vector2Int DebugPixel = new Vector2Int(700, 400);
    private const int DEBUG_BUFFER_FLOATS = 128;

    class RaymarchPass : ScriptableRenderPass
    {
        private ComputeShader _compute;
        private ComputeShader _computeStripped;
        private ComputeShader _computeMemoryProbe;
        private int _debugMode;
        private bool _forceRes;
        private int _gateW, _gateH;

        class ComputePassData
        {
            public ComputeShader compute;
            public Camera cam;
            public TextureHandle target;
            public int dispatchWidth;
            public int dispatchHeight;
            public GraphicsBuffer clipmapBuffer;
            public GraphicsBuffer brickDataBuffer;
            public GraphicsBuffer debugBuffer;
            public Vector3Int windowDimsBricks;
            public Vector3Int windowDimsChunks;
            public Vector3Int windowOriginBricks;
            public int contentCeilingVoxelY;
            public Vector2Int debugPixel;
            public int debugMode;
            public int traversalMode;
            public int useDevColors;
            public int maxOuterIterations;
            public bool useStripped;
            public bool useMemoryProbe;
            public int probeIterations;

            public GraphicsBuffer airMip1;
            public GraphicsBuffer airMip2;
            public GraphicsBuffer airMip3;
            public GraphicsBuffer airMip4;
            public Vector3Int airMipDims0;
            public Vector3Int airMipDims1;
            public Vector3Int airMipDims2;
            public Vector3Int airMipDims3;
            public int airMipLevelCount;

            public GraphicsBuffer airMipPacked;
            public Vector4[] mipInfo;
            public int usePackedMips;
            public float maxRayDistance;

            public GraphicsBuffer clipmapTier1;
            public GraphicsBuffer brickDataTier1;
            public Vector3Int windowDimsCoarseTier1;
            public Vector4 cascadeTierInfo1;
            public GraphicsBuffer clipmapTier2;
            public GraphicsBuffer brickDataTier2;
            public Vector3Int windowDimsCoarseTier2;
            public Vector4 cascadeTierInfo2;
            public Vector4 tierOuterRangeVoxels;
            public int useLODCascade;
        }

        class BlitPassData { public TextureHandle source; }
